analysis.title: Americas Real Estate: REITs: NAREIT Meeting Takeaways
key_insights: Ventas (VTR, Buy): management cited about 7% RevPOR growth at highly occupied senior housing communities versus about 5% across the portfolio. It expects pricing to stay a lever as occupancy rises, provided operators have the confidence and service quality to support higher rents.

Ventas is pushing an operator culture change through pricing data, expense benchmarks, operator comparisons, annual awards and published rankings. Management described this as new for an industry unaccustomed to 92% occupancy, let alone 100%.

Ventas said the quarter's incremental margin was about 53%. Low-50s flow-through is consistent with low-90s occupancy, and many higher-occupancy communities already earn 70% or better. Management said the path from 50% to 70% is not linear.

Invitation Homes (INVH, Buy): keeping this year's disposition pace and using proceeds for buybacks would require a different tax approach. Net operating losses from the Starwood Waypoint Homes merger are nearly exhausted and 1031 exchanges are less likely as acquisitions slow. Sustaining the 2027 level of capital return would likely need a special dividend or corporate taxes on home-sale gains (the latter viewed as unlikely).

INVH home sales are getting harder. Buyers negotiate more, days on market are rising, and cap rates have moved from the 4s into the 5s in some markets. Management sees sale opportunities in Southern California and South Florida but will not accept deep discounts to accelerate dispositions.

INVH single-family rental supply: builder deliveries are projected down 47% from the 2024 peak in 2027 and down about 65% in INVH markets. Large-operator for-lease listings are down 12% but overall listings are up 3%, and shadow supply in INVH markets is roughly flat year over year. Unsold new homes are up 50% versus seasonal normal and some may convert to rental.

UDR (UDR, Sell): the company now sets renewals using resident-level data rather than only the market rent of a vacant unit. Fourth-quarter renewal offers went out at 5.5% to 6% growth, with at least 50 basis points more expected in achieved growth. Turnover fell another 300 basis points year over year.

UDR said its 2027 rent-growth earn-in roughly doubles by region. West Coast is 180 to 200 basis points versus about 100 entering 2026, East Coast is 80 to 100 versus about 50, and Sunbelt is -75 versus -150. The full 2027 outlook still depends on when new rent growth arrives.

UDR estimated private-market apartment values fell about 10% or slightly more for the lowest-quality assets over 90 days, versus mid-single-digit declines for the highest quality. Trophy assets may trade inside a 5% cap rate, ordinary 20-year-old assets near 5.5%, and Class C or poor locations near 6% or higher. Higher rates reduce refinancing proceeds and may pressure some owners to sell.

Omega Healthcare (OHI, Buy): management cited two or three potential active portfolio-management opportunities and a full-year contribution from the PACS transaction potentially by late-February or March. It framed about 5% AFFO growth after debt-refinancing headwinds as a good outcome, versus 6% to 7% in a typical year.
OHI skilled nursing: private-market demand makes conventional acquisitions difficult. Management has had success stepping into failed or over-leveraged transactions and continues to evaluate more.

OHI triple-net-to-RIDEA conversions: management sees a selective opportunity, mainly in the UK, but expects to pass on about 80% of proposals because operators seek a premium. A recently completed conversion carries about a 26% initial return, and an offer on a potential second portfolio is well below the owner's expectation.

OHI reimbursement risk after the midterm elections: management said reimbursement rates could fall in certain states and hurt operator rent coverage. It is reviewing exposure state by state and framed dispositions and redeployment into lower-risk assets as proactive protection.

Mid-America Apartments (MAA, Neutral): management estimated a 6 to 7 cent fully loaded 2027 drag from developments delivered in 2026 still in lease-up. Including 2025 deliveries, which add 4 to 5 cents of benefit, the net 2027 impact is about 2 cents dilutive. More of the lease-up benefit is expected in 2028.

MAA 2027 guidance will be more cautious on demand because demand undershot initial 2026 expectations. Deliveries in its markets should be similar in 2027 versus 2026, except Raleigh, Nashville and Charlotte, which could be somewhat higher.
GS price targets: VTR $113, INVH $33, UDR $34, OHI $60, MAA $123. All are 12-month targets based on Q5-Q8 FFO multiples.

market_movers.rationale: Target is $113, up from $112 on 6 Aug 2026, based on a 24.1x Q5-Q8 FFO multiple. Management points to rent growth from higher occupancy and incremental margins above 50%.
Target is unchanged at $33 from 20 Oct 2026, based on a 15.4x Q5-Q8 FFO multiple. Supply is improving but home sales and capital return funding are harder.
Target is $34, down from $35 on 20 Oct 2026, based on a 13.0x Q5-Q8 FFO multiple. Renewal and earn-in data are improving but rates and cap rates are rising.
Target is $60, down from $61 on 6 Aug 2026, based on a 17.2x Q5-Q8 FFO multiple. AFFO growth is about 5% in 2027 and reimbursement risk is being reviewed state by state.
Target is $123, down from $125 on 20 Oct 2026, based on a 14.5x Q5-Q8 FFO multiple. Development lease-up weighs on 2027 FFO and demand is below initial expectations.

sector_views.rationale: VTR and OHI are both rated Buy. Pricing power at high occupancy supports VTR and OHI sees portfolio and acquisition opportunities. Ratings are relative to the GS coverage universe.
UDR is rated Sell and MAA Neutral. Rent-growth earn-in is improving but private-market values are falling and development weighs on MAA.
INVH is rated Buy as new supply declines, offset by weaker home-sale conditions.

earnings_insights: VTR: management commentary on the latest quarter put incremental margin at about 53%. This is a management figure from the meeting, not a reported-versus-adjusted earnings number.

UDR: management says 2027 rent-growth earn-in is roughly 180 to 200 basis points on the West Coast, 80 to 100 on the East Coast and -75 in the Sunbelt. Fourth-quarter renewal offers were 5.5% to 6%, with at least 50 basis points more expected in achieved growth. These are management expectations.
OHI: management framed about 5% 2027 AFFO growth after debt-refinancing headwinds as a good outcome, versus 6% to 7% in a typical year. This is management's view, not a consensus or reported figure.

MAA: management estimated a 6 to 7 cent fully loaded 2027 FFO drag from 2026 developments and about 2 cents net dilution after 2025 deliveries. About $370 million of development was delivered or is delivering in 2026. These are management estimates.
risk_factors: VTR downside: worse-than-expected SHOP occupancy growth, weaker demand, lower acquisitions or yields, and property operating expense growth.

INVH downside: greater supply pressure, weaker demand, lower acquisitions or yields, worse hurricane and natural disaster losses, property operating expense growth and the short-term interest rate path.
UDR upside risks: improved demand, higher acquisition and development volumes or yields, lower property operating expenses and a better cost of capital.

OHI downside: weaker operator health, lower acquisitions or yields, higher property operating expenses, spread compression and negative regulatory impacts. Management also flagged state reimbursement cuts after the midterms.
MAA upside and downside: supply pressure, demand, acquisition and development yields, and property expenses could each come in better or worse than expected.
Higher interest rates reduce refinancing proceeds for leveraged apartment owners and may force more distressed sales.

tension_points.bull_case: UDR's renewal offers went out at 5.5% to 6%, turnover fell 300 basis points and 2027 earn-in roughly doubles in the West and East regions.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher rates and cap rates cut private-market values by about 10% for the lowest-quality assets and reduce refinancing proceeds for leveraged owners. The report rates UDR Sell.
tension_points.what_invalidates: UDR cautioned that the full 2027 outlook depends on when new rent growth arrives. A delay in new-lease rent growth would undercut the earn-in case.

tension_points.bull_case: Builder deliveries are projected down 47% from the 2024 peak in 2027 and down about 65% in INVH markets, with shadow supply roughly flat in INVH markets.
tension_points.bear_case: Unsold new homes are up 50% versus seasonal normal and some may convert to rental. Overall for-lease listings are up 3% and shadow supply is hard to measure.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Unsold new homes converting to rentals at scale would add supply and break the improving-supply case.

theme_stances.key_argument: Pricing can stay a lever as occupancy rises if operators can support higher rents.
Higher rates and cap rates are lowering private-market apartment values and reducing refinancing proceeds for leveraged owners.
